S28.01.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact that contains code, and a folder open in VS Code to keep the result
S28.01.note: The artifact opens through a content provider (agi-artifact scheme) and the code sets no read-only flag, but the app has no code path that saves that document back to its source; the keep step is Save into the workspace. Whether typed edits persist was not verified.
steps: In the AGI Code sidebar, click the button labelled More actions (the … icon in the header).
Click Artifacts, then pick an artifact in the list (the placeholder text reads Open an artifact…).
Click inside the code and type a line; check that the text changes and can be edited.
Hover the row's save icon labelled Save into the workspace and click it to keep the result; check that a saved file opens in the editor, as in Expected.
S28.01.where: More actions (…) > Artifacts > Open an artifact… > pick an artifact with code

S28.05.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact that contains code
S28.05.note: The app sets the editor language from the artifact (artifactEditorLanguage in artifactPresentation.ts); highlighting and indentation come from VS Code, not from app code.
steps: In the AGI Code sidebar, click the button labelled More actions (the … icon in the header).
Click Artifacts, then pick an artifact that contains code (the placeholder text reads Open an artifact…).
Look at the opened editor tab: the code should show colours for keywords and strings, as in Expected.
Click at the end of a line that opens a bracket and press Return; check that indentation and matching brackets follow the language.
S28.05.where: More actions (…) > Artifacts > Open an artifact… > pick an artifact with code

S28.26.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact that contains code, and a folder open in VS Code (without one the app shows: open a folder first)
S28.26.note: Open Published Artifact opens a web share link in the browser and is not a coding workspace; the coding path is Save into the workspace.
steps: In the AGI Code sidebar, click the button labelled More actions (the … icon in the header).
Click Artifacts, then pick an artifact that contains code (the placeholder text reads Open an artifact…).
Hover the row's save icon, whose tooltip reads Save into the workspace, and click it.
In the save dialog, keep the suggested file name and click Save; check that the file opens in a normal editor tab in the open folder, ready to keep developing.
S28.26.where: More actions (…) > Artifacts > Open an artifact… > hover the row's save icon and click Save into the workspace
